question.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,1,5⟩+w⟨-2,-5,4⟩,\,Π:r=⟨-5,4,2⟩+s⟨0,3,1⟩+t⟨2,0,1⟩.
$$
question.worked_solution:
From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vectors to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨0,3,1⟩\times ⟨2,0,1⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|k \\  & =3i+2j-6k \\  & =⟨3,2,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =⟨-5,4,2⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =-19.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3,1,5⟩+w⟨-2,-5,4⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =-19 \\ ⟨3-2w,1-5w,5+4w⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =-19 \\ 3(3-2w)+2(1-5w)-6(5+4w) & =-19 \\ 9-6w+2-10w-30-24w & =-19 \\ -40w & =0 \\ w & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=0$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨3-2(0),1-5(0),5+4(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,1,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(3,1,5).$
